contracts.name: rev_net_raises_refresh_k20_liquid500_v1
contracts.selector: rank by net analyst price-target raises over the trailing 90 days (raises minus cuts, per broker; an event is usable from max(anndats, actdats) + 1 trading day); names with zero events are not eligible
contracts.universe: top 500 US common stocks by median 63-session dollar volume, price >= the xs_ranker floor, >= 1 target event in the last 365 days
contracts.construction: top 20, equal weight, gross 1.0, long only, no leverage, no stops
contracts.rebalance: monthly, first session after month-end; the member list is REFRESHED every month (the frozen revision_flow_v0 list keeps running as its own book)
contracts.fill_convention: decide on month-end close data; trade at the next session's open
contracts.costs: 10 bps one-way on traded weight (20 bps sensitivity printed beside)
contracts.control: turnover-matched random twin (same k, same eligible set, same number of replacements, same costs); SPY beside
contracts.objective: terminal wealth, balanced personality; scored as net minus twin, by year, leave-one-year-out
inputs: live analyst target events (yfinance upgrades/downgrades panel; IBES when available)
contracts.worst_case_dollars: 20 names x 5% notional, no stops: a -30% gap on one name = -1.5% of equity; gross 100%
contracts.evidence: family_board_20261110T163318Z.json liquid500/rev_net_raises k=20: +0.57%/mo vs twin, t 2.94, MDE 0.54, 18/26 years, LOO worst +0.50, breadth worst +0.27 (k=100); decay_factors_20261110T164325Z.json: edge halves after one month, gone by month 3; FF5+UMD alpha +0.50 t 1.60 MDE 0.87 = cannot distinguish from momentum + size
contracts.why: the most robust family on survivor-free CRSP 2000-2024 and the one the five leader books already trade; the decay test says a frozen list keeps about half the edge after a month, so the testable change is the monthly refresh

contracts.name: pruned_selector_population_v1 (virtual population, no broker)
contracts.selector: 30 single-signal roots (scripts/night/branching_sim.py SELECTORS), top 20 each, eligible universe
contracts.construction: each branch equal weight; population book = equal weight over surviving branches
contracts.branching_rule: kill the bottom 25% (age >= 24 months) by mean net-minus-twin since birth; the top 6 each spawn one mutant (k in {10,20,50} or the other universe); the 3 lowest-error-correlation top pairs spawn a rank-average join; children score only after birth; cap 80
contracts.control: every branch has a turnover-matched random twin; population score = population net minus the same weights on the twins; and all 30 roots never pruned
contracts.objective: terminal wealth; score = excess over twins, never over SPY
contracts.evidence: branching_sim_20261110T1640*/T1641* (7 variants): pruning gain over never-pruned roots +0.32..+0.56 %/mo net of twins, t 2.3-3.7, MDE 0.33-0.43, 18-23/31 years, LOO worst > 0 in 7/7; the Thompson allocator adds nothing reliable
contracts.why: the CH-16 design tested on history: branches differ in alpha source, each has a twin, kills are forward-only. Pruning works on this history; the allocator is optional
